title: CHAPTER FIVE. On the satisfaction of Christ: definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): On ye satisfaction belonging toward Christ. — CHAPTER FIVE. — Here, after ye states belonging toward Christ, follows SATISFACTION, by which ye Son belonging toward God, incarnate by ye grace belonging toward mercy from ye Father through ye power belonging toward ye Holy Spirit, granted toward us as Sponsor belonging toward ye better covenant, and paying Himself as ye price belonging toward redemption toward us, by His perfect obedience found in humiliation, truly and fully compensated ye disobedience belonging toward ye human race, and so merited and effected that, ye justice belonging toward GOD being preserved, all sinners who believe in Him actually obtain remission belonging toward sins and eternal life, while ye rest, if they repent and believe, can certainly obtain it. — Mark 10:45. — Matthew 20:28; — Revelation 5:9; — 2 Peter 2:1; — 2:24; — 1 Peter 1:18-19; — 10:12; — 9:12; — Hebrews 7:22; — 1 Timothy 2:6; — 1 Thessalonians 1:10; — Colossians 1:14; — 5:2; — Ephesians 1:7; — John 1:29; — Isaiah 53:4; — 2 Corinthians 5:21; — 15:22; — 1 Corinthians 1:30; — 8:1; — 5:6,9,16-19; — Ye seat belonging toward this principle stands as Romans 3:24-25;
pass_b_english: CHAPTER FIVE. On the satisfaction of Christ.

Here, after the states of Christ, follows SATISFACTION, by which the Son of God, incarnate by the grace of mercy from the Father through the power of the Holy Spirit, granted to us as Sponsor of the better covenant, and paying Himself as the price of redemption for us, by His perfect obedience found in humiliation, truly and fully compensated the disobedience of the human race, and so merited and effected that, the justice of GOD being preserved, all sinners who believe in Him actually obtain remission of sins and eternal life, while the rest, if they repent and believe, can certainly obtain it.

The seat of this principle is Romans 3:24-25; 5:6,9,16-19; 8:1; 1 Corinthians 1:30; 15:22; 2 Corinthians 5:21; Isaiah 53:4; John 1:29; Ephesians 1:7; 5:2; Colossians 1:14; 1 Thessalonians 1:10; 1 Timothy 2:6; Hebrews 7:22; 9:12; 10:12; 1 Peter 1:18-19; 2:24; 2 Peter 2:1; Revelation 5:9; Matthew 20:28; Mark 10:45.
source_text: CAPUT QUINTUM, De satisfactione Christi. Hic de statibus Christi sequitur SATISFACTIO, qua Filius Dei per gratiam miserationis a Patre virtute Spiritus sancti incarnatus nobis in melioris foederis Sponforem concessus, seque in pretium redemtionis pro nobis dependens, perfecta obedientia sui, quae in humiliatione reperitur, inobedientiam humani generis vere ac plene compensavit, adeoque meritus est & effecit, ut salva DEI iustitia, omnes peccatores in ipsum credentes remissionem peccatorum & vitam aeternam actu consequerentur, ceteri vero, si resipiscerent & crederent, certo consequi possent. Sedes huius principii est Rom. 3:24-25; 5:6,9,16-19; 8:1; 1 Cor. 1:30; 15:22; 2 Cor. 5:21; Isa. 53:4; Joh. 1:29; Eph. 1:7; 5:2; Col. 1:14; 1 Thess. 1:10; 1 Tim. 2:6; Heb. 7:22; 9:12; 10:12; 1 Pet. 1:18-19; 2:24; 2 Pet. 2:1; Apoc. 5:9; Matth. 20:28; Marci 10:45.
